Requirements and candidates

Every requirement in a draft spec and every candidate requirement proposed by a research packet, in one table. Candidates are statements a packet found support for in shipped files or decompiled code; they are not yet draft specs and none is released. Released subsets are listed in the handoff index. Each row links to its source section, which owns the evidence and limits.

REQ-BROWSER-INDEX-005SPEC-BROWSER-INDEX
Draft spec		item binding: An entry of a user folder's sidecar applies to the file directly inside that folder whose name is exactly the entry's filePath; an entry that contains /, names a folder or names nothing matches no item, does not affect other entries, and is dropped from the application's copy of the sidecar, which is then marked changed. - **Static-derived (review finding RVB-01; the reviewer's binding check was re-run for this revision).** For a user folder's sidecar (resource folder), the reader matches entries by name against the files directly inside the folder that contains the sidecar folder. REQ-BROWSER-INDEX-006SPEC-BROWSER-INDEX
Draft spec		tag and color values: Each non-empty keywords entry gives the item that tag, and an item's tags are the set of these texts; each non-empty colors entry is read as an unsigned decimal number of which only the low 32 bits are kept, a resulting value n from 1 to 7 gives the item color label n, and other values and empty entries are ignored. - **Static-derived (review findings F3 and RVB-06).** The color rule. The conversion skips leading white space, accepts a sign and stops at the first non-digit, without checking the rest of the text. So 03, 3 and 3x give label 3, 4294967298 (2^32 + 2) gives label 2, andraftwiki/specs/browser-index.md

REQ-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING-002SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING

REQ-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING-003SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING
Draft spec		Settled host DryWet (conditional S, C1): For Amp and Cabinet at settled d in [0,1], let wet gain be sin(d*pi/2) and dry gain be sqrt(1-wet_gain^2). Each output channel combines its dry sample with its wet sample using those gains. Endpoint d=0 is dry, d=1 is wet; d=0.5 gives equal weights sqrt(0.5). This is the steady mathematical gain law; sample-exact floating rounding and the transition after changing d are ungraded (REQ-012).draftwiki/specs/bundled-device-hosting.md
REQ-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING-004SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-HOSTING
Draft spec		Control-change delivery (U): The audio/behavior produced by repeated control changes and their timing remains unresolved. Recovered pending-control coalescing, first-arrival order and delivery count do not establish an application-observable UI/automation interval or a required candidate queue. Model checks BDH-010/011 retain the source transformation; a candidate must not fail solely because its equivalent output uses another order, count or control-update mechanism. Parameter domains/conversions retain their canonical owner.draftwiki/specs/bundled-device-hosting.md

REQ-CLIP-LAUNCH-012SPEC-CLIP-LAUNCH
Draft spec		follow-chance rescaling on load: - **X (path S; assumes A2, A3).** After a clip's follow action is read, with A and B its stored chances (32-bit floats): - if A = 0 and B = 0 (−0 counts as 0): chance A becomes 100, chance B stays 0, and follow actions become disabled; - otherwise: chance A becomes round(A ÷ ((A + B) ÷ 100)) and chance B becomes 100 − chance A. The arithmetic is 32-bit float, and halves round away from zero. - Each new chance is then limited to 0 to 100 by the chance setter (A7, settled). - **X.** Examples: 30/30 → 50/50; 1/2 → 33/67; 1/7 → 13/87; 1/0 → 100/0; 3/5 → 38/62 and 5/3 → 63/37 (halves); 1/199 → 1/99draftwiki/specs/clip-launch.md

Draft spec		follow-time rounding on load: - **X (path S; assumes A2, A3).** After load, a clip's FollowTime is rounded to the grid of 1/3,843,840 beat, halves away from zero, by the binary64 formula of REQ-MIDI-NOTE-STORAGE-006: with h the binary64 value of 1/3,843,840 and s = +1 for x ≥ 0 (including −0), else −1, the held value is s × (⌊|x + s × h/2| × 3,843,840⌋ / 3,843,840). The values ±1.7976931348623155e308, the largest finite value and +∞ are not rounded. Examples: 2.0000001 → 2; 3.0000002 → 11,531,521/3,843,840 (≈ 3.00000026); 1e-8 → 0; −0 → +0. 3,843,840 = 2⁸·3·5·7·11·13, so every triplet and bar length of REQ-015 is a wholedraftwiki/specs/clip-launch.md

REQ-DR-ECHO-002SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Delay units and Sync Mode: **D12.** Delay time is in beat divisions with Sync on and milliseconds with Sync off. REQ-DR-ECHO-003SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Stereo Link and offsets: **D12.** Stereo Link propagates time, Sync-switch and Sync-Mode edits to both delay lines; Offset remains independent per line. The initial value chosen on linking is U. Evidence: echo:B006, echo:B007.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-ECHO-004SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Input gain and dry distortion: **D12.** Input adjusts gain applied to the dry signal; D applies distortion to it. The distortion curve, clipping threshold and gain location beyond this description remain U. Evidence: echo:B008.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-ECHO-005SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Feedback and inversion: **D12.** Feedback returns each channel output to delay inputs; Ø inverts output before feeding it back. This documents sign inversion, not a full gain/stability law or parity of the first repeat. Evidence: echo:B009.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-ECHO-006SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Echo Tunnel: **D12.** Echo Tunnel displays repeats progressing outside to center; spacing denotes repeat interval, white dots form a fixed eighth-note reference. Dragging the display edits delay times. Evidence: echo:B010, echo:B011, echo:B012.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-ECHO-007SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Filters and display: **D12.** Filter enables high-pass and low-pass filtering; each has cutoff and resonance. The triangle shows/hides the Filter Display, whose points also edit filters. REQ-DR-ECHO-008SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		LFO wave, rate and phase: **D12.** The Modulation tab offers sine, triangle, saw up, saw down, square and noise. Sync selects beat-based Rate versus Freq in Hz. Display dragging edits frequency; Phase offsets left/right waveforms and 180 degrees denotes opposed phase. Exact wave shapes/noise law are U. Evidence: echo:B015, echo:B016, echo:B017, [echo:B018](../draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-ECHO-009SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES

REQ-DR-ECHO-011SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Input gate and wet ducking: **D12.** Gate operates at the input and mutes components below Threshold; Release sets closing time after a drop below threshold. Evidence: echo:B024, echo:B025, [echo:B026](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/delay-reverb/manual-ecdraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md

REQ-DR-REVERB-001SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Input filters: **D12.** Input first passes through individually switchable low/high cut filters. X controls band center, Y bandwidth; sliders offer the same controls. Cutoff laws, slope and bypass transition are U. Evidence: reverb:B006.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-002SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Early reflections and Spin: **D12.** Early reflections precede the diffuse tail. Spin modulates early reflections with Amount and Rate and can be disabled. REQ-DR-REVERB-003SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Shape: **D12.** At smaller Shape values early reflections decay more gradually and diffuse onset is sooner, increasing overlap. Larger values yield quicker reflection decay and later diffuse onset. No continuous mapping or exact onset/decay metric follows. Evidence: reverb:B010.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-004SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Diffuse tail and shelving: **D12.** The Diffusion Network generates the tail. Independent high/low shelving filters shape frequency-dependent decay and can be turned off. Filter transfer, decay multipliers and frequency equality are U. Evidence: reverb:B012, reverb:B013.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-005SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Diffusion and Scale: **D12.** Diffusion and Scale control tail density/coarseness, with pronounced coloration at extremely small room Size. No delay-line topology or parameter law is established. Evidence: reverb:B014.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-006SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Chorus: **D12.** Chorus modulates the diffusion with Amount and Rate and has an independent disable switch. Exact oscillator phases, waves and reset state are U. Evidence: reverb:B016.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-007SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Predelay: **D12.** Predelay is in milliseconds before the first early reflection. The manual describes 1-25 ms as typical natural-room choices; this is not its allowed range or rounding rule. Evidence: reverb:B018.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-008SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Size and Smooth: **D12.** Size controls virtual room volume. Smooth None changes diffusion delay times immediately; Slow/Fast update them over a period. Exact periods, interpolation and transition ordering are U. Evidence: reverb:B019, reverb:B020.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-009SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Decay definition: **D12.** Decay denotes time for tail amplitude to fall to 1/1000 of its initial amplitude (-60 dB). Draft spec		Freeze, Flat and Cut: **D12.** Freeze sustains the diffuse response almost endlessly. With Freeze on, Flat bypasses high/low shelves; Flat off permits energy loss in attenuated bands according to shelf state. Cut prevents new input contributing to frozen reverberation; Cut off admits it. No exact infinite tail or bypass law outside Freeze follows. Evidence: reverb:B022.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-REVERB-011SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Stereo, Density and output: **D12.** Stereo lowest setting mixes output to mono; 120 degrees describes independent reverberant channels. No coefficient matrix, CPU count or mix law is specified. Evidence: reverb:B023, reverb:B024, [reverb:B026](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/fudraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md

REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-001SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Wet send and predelay: **D12.** Send changes gain feeding reverb while leaving dry signal unaffected. Predelay offers time/beat-synced units; each mode has an independent Feedback setting. These are distinct from the algorithm additional Delay. Timing units, feedback persistence across mode toggles and sample conversion need separate evidence. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B007, hybrid-reverb:B010, [hybrid-reverb:B011](../../analysdraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-002SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Serial routing: **D12.** Serial sends convolution output into the algorithm engine. The convolution stays active; Blend 100/0 gives convolution-only output, while 0/100 gives algorithmic output fed by convolution. It is not raw-input algorithm-only at the second endpoint. The interpolation law is U. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B013, hybrid-reverb:B014, [hybrid-reverb:B019](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/dedraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-003SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Parallel routing: **D12.** Parallel keeps convolution and algorithm engines separate. Blend 100/0 gives pure convolution and 0/100 pure algorithmic output. Exact summation/gain law is U. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B015, hybrid-reverb:B019.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-004SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Single-engine routing and disabled controls: **D12.** Algorithm uses only the algorithm engine; Convolution only convolution. Unused-engine controls are grayed out. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B016, hybrid-reverb:B017, [hybrid-reverb:B018](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/delay-reverb/manual-hybrid-reverb-blocksdraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-005SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		IR selection and display: **D12.** Category and IR selectors choose impulses; arrows advance continuously across category boundaries. Waveform reflects Attack/Decay/Size changes. Ten documented categories are Early Reflections, Real Places, Chambers and Large Rooms, Made for Drums, Halls, Plates, Springs, Bigger Spaces, Textures and User. Exact installed IR list/version is U. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B021, hybrid-reverb:B022, [hydraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-006SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		User IR import and removal: **D12.** Dropping an audio file on the waveform adds it as an IR; audio siblings in its folder are also added. Remove the device and add it again: previously added User samples no longer appear in User until added again. This does not define saved-Set restoration, supported codec set, recursion, file sorting or cleanup of source bytes. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B003, hybrid-reverb:B024.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-007SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Convolution envelope: **D12.** Attack/Decay control the IR amplitude envelope attack/decay times; Size controls relative IR size. Exact envelope, resampling, normalization, latency and stereo-channel convolution are U. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B025.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-008SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Algorithms and common controls: **D12.** Algorithms are Dark Hall, Quartz, Shimmer, Tides and Prism, with controls changing by selection. All have Decay, Size, Delay and Freeze. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B027, hybrid-reverb:B028, [hybrid-reverb:B029](../draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-009SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Freeze versus Freeze In: **D12.** Freeze blocks input to the algorithmic engine and sets decay to infinite for sustained output. Freeze In adds new input to frozen reverberation. This contract is algorithmic; it does not establish freezing convolution output, state persistence or numerical infinite duration. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B031.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-010SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Dark Hall controls: **D12.** Dark Hall provides Damping for high-frequency filtering, Mod for tail movement, Shape from small/resonant toward large/diffused, Bass X low-tail crossover and Bass Mult low-tail decay scaling. Long decay with tiny Size can give gong-like resonance; no guaranteed timbre or crossover law follows. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B034, hybrid-reverb:B036, [hybrid-reverb:B037](../../analysis/ableton-live-12draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-011SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Quartz controls: **D12.** Quartz provides Damping (high filtering), Lo Damp (low filtering), Mod (tail movement), Diffusion (sparse to dense) and Distance (closer/denser to farther/more-spaced reflections). Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B043, hybrid-reverb:B045, [hybrid-reverb:B046](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/delay-reverb/manual-hydraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-012SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Shimmer controls and zero amount: **D12.** Shimmer includes Damping, Mod, Diffusion, Pitch in semitones and Shimmer amount. Size affects spacing of echoes on percussive material. No resampling, diffusion threshold kernel or feedback stability law is specified. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B051, [hybrid-reverb:B053](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/delay-reverb/manual-hybrid-revdraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-013SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Tides modulation: **D12.** Tides modulates output spectrum with a multiband filter. Random spectra and phase/timing precision are U. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B060, hybrid-reverb:B062, [hybrid-rdraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-014SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Prism band decay controls: **D12.** Prism is described as based on spectrally flat velvet noise. Low Mult and High Mult scale respective tail-band decays; X over sets the band boundary. Evidence: hybrid-reverb:B068, hybrid-reverb:B070, [hybrid-reverb:B071](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/delay-reverb/manual-hybrid-reverb-blocks.jsondraftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-015SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		EQ placement and enable: **D12.** EQ has its own tab and toggle. REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-016SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		EQ bands: **D12.** Four EQ bands include low/high bands switchable between pass filters and shelves, with 6 to 96 dB/octave slope range in pass modes; two middle peak bands cover the frequency range. REQ-DR-HYBRID-REVERB-017SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Wet width and Dry/Wet: **D12.** Stereo controls wet width with mono at 0% and widening above 100%; Dry/Wet balances processed/dry audio and 100% is documented for return use. REQ-DR-RESONATORS-002SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Input filter: **D12.** Input filtering precedes resonators, with low-pass, band-pass, high-pass and notch types, and Frequency controlling selected filter frequency. Filter order, slope and switching tails are U. Evidence: resonators:B003.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-RESONATORS-003SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Decay, Const and Color: **D12.** Decay changes resonator sustain; normal pitch-dependent decay lasts longer at lower notes. Evidence: resonators:B005, resonators:B006.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-RESONATORS-004SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Channel assignments: **D12.** Resonator I receives left+right, II/IV left only, III/V right only. Summation scaling and the output stereo matrix are U. Evidence: resonators:B007.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-RESONATORS-005SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Root tuning and context: **D12.** Without scale awareness/tuning, I sets root and others follow musical intervals. With scale awareness, I is relative to active clip scale in octave 2; others relative to I. With tuning active, I uses an absolute tuning-defined pitch and others relative to it. Exact tuning precedence, no-active-clip fallback and changes during a tail remain U. Evidence: resonators:B008, resonators:B009.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md
REQ-DR-RESONATORS-006SPEC-DELAY-REVERB-DEVICES
Draft spec		Note, Fine and relative ranges: **D12.** Default Note is semitones C-1 to C5; scale awareness changes to scale degrees, tuning to note indices. Fine I edits cents. II-V transpose relative to I by ±24 semitones or ±21 scale degrees and have individual Fine controls. Note-label ranges do not establish internal numbering, quantization or frequency calculation. Evidence: resonators:B009, resonators:B011.draftwiki/specs/delay-reverb-devices.md

REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-001SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		installed vocabulary and examples: **D-installed / E3–E5.** The installed schema declares Audio Effect, MIDI Effect, Instrument and Drum rack classes. Each declares sixteen macro control fields, visibility count, randomization and snapshot exclusions, a chain list and macro variations. ZoneRange declares minimum, maximum and two crossfade bounds; MacroSnapshot declares sixteen values and sixteen presence flags. The retained Suite demo contains respectively 23, 1, 8 and 1 rack occurrences. The retained slicing preset contains five snapshots. These are documentary assertions, not load/save or semantic rules for the private field draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-002SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		rack type and legal signal placement: **D12 / E1 §25.2.** MIDI Effect Racks hold MIDI effects on MIDI tracks. Audio Effect Racks hold audio effects on audio paths, including after an instrument on a MIDI track. Instrument and Drum chains order MIDI effects before an instrument and audio effects after it. Invalid placement is outside the documented valid configuration; exact drag rejection, relocation, replacement and malformed-file responses are U. This does not resolve the file-reader question in REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-012.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-003SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		serial, parallel and nested flow: **D12 / E1 §25.1.1.** Devices within a chain process left to right. Instrument and effect rack chains receive the same input in parallel subject to their zones; their outputs combine at the rack output, then feed downstream devices. Drum chains receive assigned notes instead (REQ-016). A rack may contain racks and acts as a device in the enclosing chain. Exact summation, ordering of coincident MIDI events, latency and maximum practical nesting depth are U.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-004SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		creation, grouping and dismantling: **D12 / E1 §25.2.** Loading a generic rack creates an empty rack. Group selected devices, Group to Drum Rack and grouping existing chains create enclosing racks; repeated grouping can nest them. Selecting a rack title and Ungroup dismantles that rack. The manual does not define flattening/routing resolution for every multi-chain or return-containing rack; those outcomes are U.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-005SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		chain list and selection: **D12 / E1 §§25.3–25.4.1.** Dropping devices, presets or chains in the chain-list drop area adds chains. Selecting a chain shows its devices; multiple selections show their count. Chains expose activator, solo and hot-swap; audio-output rack chains also expose volume/pan. Rack-title selection addresses the whole rack for move/copy/delete. Auto Select selects chains currently processing signals; Drum Rack selection follows receipt of the assigned note. Exact solo/activator audio interaction, selection expiry and contention with manual selection are U. Rack view selectors show or hide eligible Mdraftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-006SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		available zone filters: **D12 / E1 §§25.5–25.5.1.** Instrument and MIDI Effect Racks have key, velocity and selector zones; a note enters a chain only if it passes all three. Audio Effect Racks have selector zones, without MIDI key/velocity zones. Drum Racks have no zone editor; their Receive choosers filter notes. All matching parallel chains can receive the same qualifying input.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-007SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		zone editing and ranges: **D12 / E1 §§25.5–25.5.4.1.** Zones can be moved and resized, with separately editable fades. Key zones cover selected MIDI keys; velocity zones use Note On velocities 1–127. The selector scale is 0–127; the documented initial selector zone is the single value 0. Multiple chains may share ranges. Exact rounding, edge inclusion for resized ranges, out-of-range edits and MIDI velocity-zero interpretation are U here; note encoding belongs to MIDI note storage. Key, Velocity and Chain buttons select their editors; Hide hides them. Main and fade sections resize from their redraftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-008SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		fade destination: **D12 / E1 §§25.5.2–25.5.4.** Key/velocity fades attenuate incoming note velocity. Selector fades in a MIDI Effect Rack attenuate note velocity. Selector fades in Instrument and Audio Effect Racks attenuate chain output audio. Exact fade law, rounding to MIDI velocity, overlap normalization and treatment of a zero-length fade are U; no linear or equal-power equation is specified.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-009SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		selector filtering of controllers: **D12 / E1 §25.5.4.** Instrument and MIDI Effect Rack selector zones filter notes by default, allowing other MIDI events such as controllers through. Enabling Chain Selector Filters MIDI Ctrl makes the selector filter all MIDI events. Held-note release routing and sustain/channel-mode edge cases remain U.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-010SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		selector movement and existing tails: **D12 / E1 §25.5.4.** For an audio-output chain with a fade ending its selector zone, moving outside attenuates the output to zero. With no fade, leaving the selector zone does not attenuate existing output; an existing effect tail may finish according to that effect. This distinction does not specify audio effect input admission, voice lifetime, clicks, smoothing or compensation changes.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-011SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		macro count and visibility: **D12 / E1 §25.7; E2 §§23.2.3,23.2.6.1.** A rack supports up to sixteen macros; a newly created factory rack, with no custom default or loaded preset, shows eight. Visibility controls change the number shown; shown/hidden state is saved with the Set. Hidden-control mapping activity and lower visibility bound are U. E3 corroborates sixteen storage slots, without proving runtime limits.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-012SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		mapping and ranges: **D12 / E1 §25.7.1.** Entering Macro Map Mode highlights mappable controls, shows macro Map buttons and opens the Mapping Browser. Select a contained parameter, then a macro's Map button to create an assignment; one macro can address several parameters. Min/Max refine each assignment; Min greater than Max inverts it, and Invert Range reverses the current range. Assignments can be edited/deleted in that browser; leaving Map Mode ends this editing mode. Exact interpolation, quantized parameters and out-of-domain mappings are U.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-013SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		delegated control and macro display: **D12 / E1 §25.7.1.** A mapped device parameter is disabled for direct control; clip-envelope modulation remains possible. A single mapping supplies its name and units to the macro by default. Multiple mappings restore the generic macro name regardless of whether their units match, absent a separately applied custom name. Multiple mappings use 0–127 units unless every target has the same unit type and range; in that case, the common units and range are retained. Custom names/colors/info text are editable. This last clause does not assert an automatic exclusion after every new volume mapping. Draft spec		variations: **D12 / E1 §25.7.3.** New stores current macro state as a variation, initially named sequentially Variation 1, Variation 2, and so on. Variations can be renamed, duplicated and deleted. Launch recalls a stored state; Overwrite replaces it with the current state. Exclude Macro From Variations prevents that control changing on launch; disabling the exclusion restores participation. Draft spec		dropping onto pads: **D12 / E1 §25.6.1.** Each pad denotes a MIDI note. With factory dropping defaults, a sample on an empty pad creates a chain with Simpler. Custom dropping defaults are outside this clause; failed-load atomicity is U. Independently compatible browser instruments and presets can also be dropped onto pads; this does not establish arbitrary browser-object admission or new sample-dropping defaults.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-019SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		pad distribution, swapping and layering: **D12 / E1 §25.6.1.** Multiple samples dropped normally populate chromatically upward from the destination, replacing samples while preserving effects. Alt-drag on Windows / Cmd-drag on macOS layers them in a nested Instrument Rack. Dragging a pad to another swaps note assignments; existing clips keep their notes and therefore address the new sounds. The same platform modifier layers both pads' chains in a nested Instrument Rack. Overflow above note 127, sample ordering within a multiselection and effects during failed loads are U.draftwiki/specs/device-racks.md

Draft spec		pads represent notes, including multiple chains: **D12 / E1 §25.6.1.** The 128-note pad map shows groups of sixteen. Changing Receive updates pad presentation; matching chains, including nested ones, respond to the note. A one-chain pad shows that chain's name and permits rename/hot-swap. A multiple-chain pad displays Multi; mute/solo/preview address all its chains, rename/hot-swap are disabled, and delete removes all those chains. Exact mixed mute/solo icon semantics and controller scrolling protocols are U. The pad overview can be dragged or navigated with focused up/down keys; Alt Windows/Cmd macOS shifts by single rows. Configured devices/Racks or existing admitted presets can be dragged into the corresponding Audio to MIDI folders. A Drum Rack nested in an Instrument Rack is not recognized as a Drums default in this source context. The corresponding conversion uses the saved default; where several coexist, the last ADDED is used. Conversion owner ATM036/037 keeps factory/no-custom, genuinely NONEMPTY recognition and productive nonzero pdraftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-DEVICE-RACKS-038SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS
Draft spec		Project-specific default scope: **D12 / E2; exact-build U.** A Current Project Defaults folder and appropriate related folders can be made through Explorer Windows/Finder Mac or browser New Folder, then populated by dragging admitted devices/tracks. Plug-ins cannot be dragged directly to Current Project: the source workaround creates Plug-In Configurations/Audio Units/VSTs, saves a library configuration, moves its Default.appc-containing plug-in folder to the Project type folder, and saves again if a User Library copy is wanted. Corresponding Project defaults override User Library items when used in that Project. Context Savdraftwiki/specs/device-racks.md
REQ-SAMPLER-001SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Multisample layers and focus (D): Zone toggles a separate editor above Device View; Key/Vel/Sel select its range editor. Every contained sample is listed as a layer. Selecting a layer exposes it in the Sample tab. With Auto Select enabled, all layers eligible for the arriving note through key, velocity and selector zones are selected for that note duration. Simultaneous selection/ending-note tie behavior is unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.5 (retained HTML line 1554); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-ldraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-002SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Key and velocity eligibility (D): Each layer responds only within its key zone and Note On velocity zone. Newly imported key zones cover the full MIDI note range. Velocity zones span 1–127. The manual inconsistently describes full key coverage as “127” while naming C-2–G8; do not derive a 127-versus-128 endpoint rule from that wording. Zone-edge inclusivity and fade weighting are not independently resolved. See also velocity-zones. Evidence: manual §31.10.5.3 (retained HTML line 1700); [manual §31.10.5.4](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-003SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Sample selector latch (D): Each layer also has a 0–127 sample-select zone. A layer is eligible only if that zone overlaps the current selector. The selector affects availability at trigger time: moving it while a sample plays does not switch that playing voice to a different sample. Selector fade and exact boundary inclusivity are unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.5.5 (retained HTML line 1744); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.jsodraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-004SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Zone fades and edits (D): Zone edges resize ranges, zone bodies move them and upper corners set fades. Lin/Pow switches all zone fades between linear and constant-power modes. Range normalization on overlapping/crossed/zero-width edges, the exact gain law and endpoint rounding remain unknown; names alone do not prove sin/cos coefficients. Evidence: manual §31.10.5 (retained HTML line 1554); exact retained source locators in the heading map.draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-005SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Layer management and range distribution (D): Layer menu supports Delete, Duplicate, Rename and sorting by name/key/velocity/selector in both directions. Select All With Same Range uses the currently active editor. Distribute Ranges Equally spans C-2–G8; Around Root Key allocates ranges around differing roots without overlaps, distributing equal-root layers evenly. Exact division remainder/tie rules are unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.5.2 (retained HTML line 1678); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-1draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-006SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Round Robin modes (D): With RR enabled, layers sharing the same key zone cycle by mode. Forward goes top→bottom and wraps; Backward bottom→top and wraps. Other excludes an immediate repeat; Random permits repeats. Reset Interval restarts at its chosen musical interval: Forward from top, Backward from bottom, and Other/Random from the sample first played. These are current manual clauses only; target applicability and interactions with unequal velocity/selector ranges, one eligible layer and stopped transport remain unknown. Evidence: [manual §31.10.5.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-referdraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-007SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Per-layer sample controls (D): Sample tab values generally apply to selected layer. Root Key sets its reference note; sample Detune spans ±50 cents; Volume ranges from attenuation to +24 dB; Pan controls that sample. Reverse and RAM/interpolation are explicitly global exceptions. Sample chooser changes edited layer. Exact root mapping under tuning is unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.6 (retained HTML line 1782); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-008SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Reverse and display-only controls (D): Global Reverse plays from Sample End backwards through any active sustain loop toward Sample Start without generating a new file. Snap uses left-channel zero crossings for sample/loop points and does not ensure right-channel continuity. Vertical Zoom changes display only. B/M/L/R chooses displayed channels, without specifying any output-channel processing. Evidence: manual §31.10.6 (retained HTML line 1782); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sdraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-009SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Sample extent, sustain loop and Link (D): Sample Start/End bound playback. Without an enabled loop, Sample End terminates playback even if the volume envelope continues; active sustain/release-loop behavior is the controlling exception, as specified here and in REQ-SAMPLER-010. With no sustain loop, playback ends at Sample End or completion of envelope release. Forward sustain loops return Loop End→Loop Start; back-and-forth loops reverse at both ends. With release mode Off they keep looping during volume-envelope release. Link makes effective Sample Start equal Loop Start, disabling but retaining the original Sample Start value for rdraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-010SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Release modes and loop crossfades (D): Release modes require active sustain looping. Release Enabled proceeds linearly toward Sample End on envelope release. Release Loop mode goes to Sample End then jumps to Release Loop start; back-and-forth release reverses between those points until the volume envelope ends. Crossfade is independently available for sustain/release loops with constant-power default or title-menu linear selection; loop Detune adjusts their pitch. Exact transition at a note-off coincident with a loop edge is unknown. Evidence: [manual §31.10.6.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-011SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Envelope stages and repetition (D): Attack moves Initial→Peak; Decay Peak→Sustain; Release moves toward End on Note Off. Zero slope is linear; positive slopes move faster at the beginning, negative slopes faster at the end. Loop restarts after Decay, Beat/Sync after a musical Repeat interval; Sync aligns to song time. Trigger ignores Note Off. Velocity scales segments, not Beat/Sync beat-time. Exact curves/clock rounding remain unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.6.1 (retained HTML line 1800); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-012SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Interpolation and RAM (D): Interpolation is global, offering Normal, Good and Best quality. RAM is global and loads the entire multisample into RAM when enabled. Quality names provide no filter kernel or numeric fidelity contract. Allocation failure, streaming transition and memory-budget outcomes remain unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.6.1 (retained HTML line 1800); exact retained source locators in the heading map.draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-013SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Modulation oscillator (D): Each voice has an FM/AM modulation oscillator; its signal is not directly audible as an independent sound source. It has 21 waveform choices, modulation amount and velocity amount, plus an envelope. Fixed enables frequency Freq×Multi independent of input pitch; with Fixed off, Coarse/Fine are used. Exact waveforms, FM scaling and AM law remain unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.7.1 (retained HTML line 1888); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/fdraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-014SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Pitch envelope, zone shift and glide (D): Pitch envelope affects sample and enabled modulation oscillator; Amount sets influence in semitones. Global Transpose/Detune act in semitones/cents. Key Zone Shift changes selection of sample layers while retaining played pitch. Spread creates two detuned voices per note. Glide is mono and Portamento poly, with Time defining transition duration. Pitch paths under alternate tuning and exact portamento law are unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.7.2 (retained HTML line 1888); exact retained source locators indraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-015SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Filter and waveshaper routing (D): Filter provides low-pass/high-pass/band-pass/notch/Morph,12/24 dB and circuit choices with the same documented availability as Simpler REQ-SIMPLER-011. Its own filter envelope requires enable and nonzero Amount. Shaper offers Soft/Hard/Sine/4bit; the routing control selects shaper→filter or filter→shaper. Transfer functions and oversampling are unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.8.1 (retained HTML line 1906); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sampledraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-016SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Global articulation and voice control (D): Volume envelope articulates the instrument; Time globally scales all envelope lengths and Time<Key varies that scaling by note pitch. Global Pan and random pan act across samples. Voices allows up to32 simultaneous voices. Retrigger reuses already-playing same-note voices instead of adding them. Voice stealing order, smoothing and any counting interaction with Spread remain unknown. Evidence: manual §31.10.8.2 (retained HTML line 1906); exact retained source locators in the [heading draftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md
REQ-SAMPLER-017SPEC-DEVICE-SAMPLER
Draft spec		Auxiliary envelope and LFO routing (D): An auxiliary loopable envelope has A/B destinations and independent amounts; the manual describes29 destinations. Three LFOs expose sine/square/triangle/down-saw/up-saw/sample-and-hold,0.01–30 Hz or beat-time from1/64 note to8 bars. Retrig resets at note onset; Offset sets phase. LFO1 has Volume/Pan/Filter/Pitch amounts; LFO2/3 have A/B destinations and Phase/Spin stereo modes. Phase keeps channel rates equal; Spin can make right run up to50% faster. Exact destination enumeration and random sequences remain unknown. Evidence: [manual §31.10.9](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-insdraftwiki/specs/device-sampler.md

MPE assignment, destination clamps, simultaneous-source combination and note-off velocity handling beyond these assignments are unknown. Draft spec		Load and replace sample (D): Dropping a sample from the browser loads it. Dragging another sample or using sample Hot-Swap replaces the loaded sample. The precedence when clip start/end and loop bounds disagree is unknown. REQ-SIMPLER-002SPEC-DEVICE-SIMPLER
Draft spec		Playback mode selection (D): Expose Classic, One-Shot and Slicing modes. Classic is the documented initial mode with polyphonic playback and ADSR/looping; One-Shot is monophonic and has no looping; Slicing selects sample regions chromatically without modifying the original file. User defaults may replace initial settings. Evidence: manual §31.11.1 (retained HTML line 1984); exact retained source locators in the heading map.draftwiki/specs/device-simpler.md
REQ-SIMPLER-003SPEC-DEVICE-SIMPLER
Draft spec		Classic region and percentage controls (D): In Classic, absolute flags delimit the available region. Start and Length are percentages of that region. Length 50% selects half its duration. The Loop amount is active only while Loop is enabled. The precise Start/Length constraint and clamp rule at the region end remains unknown. Evidence: manual §31.11.1.1 (retained HTML line 2014); exact retained source locators in the heading map.draftwiki/specs/device-simpler.md
REQ-SIMPLER-004SPEC-DEVICE-SIMPLER
Draft spec		Classic looping, snap and fades (D): Loop enables repeated playback while a note is held. Snap moves region/loop markers to zero crossings using the left channel of stereo samples; it does not guarantee a click-free right channel. Fade crossfades loop endpoints. The title-bar option selects constant-power (documented default) or linear loop fades; Fade is unavailable with Warp enabled (context-menu-options-for-simpler). Exact crossfade coefficients are unknown. Evidence: manual §31.11.1.1 (retained HTML line 2014); [manual §31.11.7](httpdraftwiki/specs/device-simpler.md
REQ-SIMPLER-005SPEC-DEVICE-SIMPLER
Draft spec		Voice limits and repeated pitch (D): Voices sets the simultaneous voice limit. When exceeded, the oldest voices are removed in favor of new voices. With Retrig enabled a sustaining copy of the same note is cut on its next trigger; with Retrig disabled same-note voices can overlap. A useful audible retrigger comparison requires Voices>1 and a long release. Exact stealing fade/tie ordering is unknown. Evidence: manual §31.11.1.1 (retained HTML line 2014); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.draftwiki/specs/device-simpler.md
REQ-SIMPLER-006SPEC-DEVICE-SIMPLER
Draft spec		One-Shot Trigger, Gate and fade (D): One-Shot uses absolute region flags, has no Loop/Length/Voices controls and is always monophonic. Trigger plays the sample after note release. Gate begins Fade Out at note release and reaches silence after its configured duration. In Trigger, Fade Out is placed before the sample-region end. Fade In starts at note onset. Endpoint rounding and fade curves are unknown. Evidence: manual §31.11.1.2 (retained HTML line 2032); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-1draftwiki/specs/device-simpler.md

Draft spec		Envelopes (D): Amplitude, filter and pitch have ADSR controls, editable by values or graph handles. Draft spec		from stored values to host values: - **S** (N6). Live sends indices 0 to 129 except 2, in the N6 order. Each stored value is first clamped to its domain (SPEC-BUNDLED-DEVICE-PARAMETERS). Then: - **Polyphony** v: max(v − 1, 0) on index 0, and 1 on index 7 if v > 0.5, else 0; - **PitchBendRange** v / 12; - **Octave** v + 3; **Transpose** v + 12; - **KeyboardUnison**, **LFOSync** and **BodyType**: v + 1 when their toggle (KeyboardUnisonToggle, LFOSyncToggle, BodyToggle) is on, else 0; - **PortamentoProportional**: 1 when off, 0 draftwiki/specs/device-tension.md
REQ-DEVICE-TENSION-003SPEC-DEVICE-TENSION
Draft spec		note events and timing: - **X.** The device acts on note events on a control grid of P = ⌊fs/1000⌋ frames: 44 at 44.1 kHz and 48 at 48 kHz, counted from the first processed frame. An event at frame f takes effect at the start g of the grid period that contains f. If g lies in an earlier host block than f, the event takes effect at g + P instead. An event renders bit-identically to the same event placed at its effective frame. Tested on 560 note-ons (44.1 kHz blocks of 512, 64 and 333; 48 kHz) and 500 note-offs. - **X.** From the effective frame of a note-on, the first non-zero output frame follows after a fixed delaydraftwiki/specs/device-tension.md

Whole octaves give the shifted note's frequency exactly. Other shifts are slightly sharp, as the 2ˣ approximation A of SPEC-DEVICE-CORPUS REQ-006 predicts. REQ-DYN-MULTIBAND-DYNAMICS-001SPEC-DYNAMICS-DEVICES
Draft spec		Band count and crossovers: **D12 / E1 multiband-dynamics:B002, multiband-dynamics:B012, multiband-dynamics:B014.** Up to three bands each support Above and Below thresholds and compression/expansion. REQ-DYN-MULTIBAND-DYNAMICS-002SPEC-DYNAMICS-DEVICES
Draft spec		Activators, solos and band gain ordering: **D12 / E1 multiband-dynamics:B015.** Each band has activator/solo. Bypass need not remove crossover filtering; summation and multi-solo policy are unknown.draftwiki/specs/dynamics-devices.md
REQ-DYN-MULTIBAND-DYNAMICS-003SPEC-DYNAMICS-DEVICES

Draft spec		Threshold drag and modifiers: **D12 / E1 multiband-dynamics:B017.** Dragging the left/right block edges horizontally edits Below/Above thresholds. Numeric step, clipping and tie rules are unknown.draftwiki/specs/dynamics-devices.md

Double-click resets selected region volume to its default; that default value is not established here.draftwiki/specs/dynamics-devices.md
REQ-DYN-MULTIBAND-DYNAMICS-006SPEC-DYNAMICS-DEVICES
Draft spec		Four processing directions: **D12 / E1 multiband-dynamics:B005, multiband-dynamics:B006, multiband-dynamics:B008, multiband-dynamics:B009, multiband-dynamics:B010, multiband-dynamics:B011, multiband-dynamics:B019.** Lowering Above volume is downward compression; raising Above is upward expansion. REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-001SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		reading model: - **D.** The schema file lists each class with its fields. Each field has a class and one of four forms: a compound child element (type 0); a base value (type −4), written either as an attribute of the parent or as a child element with one Value attribute; a list or slot (type −1) whose children are elements named by their own class, each list item with an Id attribute; an array (type −3) whose items are named by the field's array class. In all 375 shipped 12.0_12402 documents every element is a field of its parent's class, every list item is a schema class, and children occur in the cladraftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-002SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		the track list: - **D.** LiveSet/Tracks holds the audio, MIDI, group and return tracks as AudioTrack, MidiTrack, GroupTrack and ReturnTrack items, in their display order. Shipped sets hold 124 MIDI, 91 audio, 20 return and 3 group tracks; in all 26 every return track follows every other track. The main and cue tracks are not in this list (REQ-004). - **S.** The set does not open when Tracks holds no player track. This includes an empty list, an absent Tracks element and a list of return tracks only. - **S.** The set does not open when a player track follows a return track. - **S.** A track whosedraftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-003SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		track Id, name and colour: - **D.** Every track item has an Id attribute, unique within Tracks. Values are arbitrary non-negative integers, not positions (12 13 8 14 2 3 in the default template). In 39 of 238 shipped tracks the value equals a pointee Id of the same set: track Ids and pointee Ids are separate spaces (REQ-015, REQ-016). - **D.** Name holds EffectiveName, UserName, Annotation and MemorizedFirstClipName, each with a Value attribute. UserName is the name the user gave and is empty in 80 of 238 tracks; EffectiveName then holds a generated text such as 1-MIDI or 2-Audio. 22 tracks havdraftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-004SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		main and cue tracks: - **D.** LiveSet/MainTrack and LiveSet/PreHearTrack (the cue, or preview, track) occur once each, after Tracks, without an Id. Shipped main tracks have EffectiveName Main and an empty UserName (26 of 26). The main track's DeviceChain holds four routings, Mixer, FreezeSequencer and DeviceChain; the cue track's holds four routings, Mixer and DeviceChain. Neither has session slots. - **D.** The main mixer holds the song tempo and time signature (REQ-TRANSPORT-STATE-001) and the crossfader ([REQ-MIXER-VALUES-0draftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-005SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		track device chain layout and routing: - **D.** Each track's DeviceChain element holds, in this order (26 of 26 sets): | Track | Children of DeviceChain | | --- | --- | | MidiTrack, AudioTrack | AutomationLanes, ClipEnvelopeChooserViewState, AudioInputRouting, MidiInputRouting, AudioOutputRouting, MidiOutputRouting, Mixer, MainSequencer, FreezeSequencer, DeviceChain | | ReturnTrack | the same up to Mixer, then DeviceChain, FreezeSequencer | | MainTrack | as ReturnTrack, with FreezeSequencer before DeviceChain | | PreHearTrack | as ReturnTrack, without FreezeSequencer | `MainSequencedraftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-006SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		session clip slots and scenes: - **D.** LiveSet/Scenes holds Scene items. The session slots of an audio or MIDI track are the ClipSlot items of DeviceChain/MainSequencer/ClipSlotList. In every shipped track the number of slots equals the number of scenes (215 of 215), and the freeze sequencer's ClipSlotList has the same number of slots (215 of 215; 350 of 350 in clip files). Scene counts run from 1 to 511. Return, main and cue tracks have no slots. - **D.** A slot is <ClipSlot Id="…"><LomId Value="0" /><ClipSlot><Value>…</Value></ClipSlot><HasStop Value="true" /></ClipSlot>. The inner ClipSlot/Value holds one draftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-007SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE
Draft spec		clip containers: - **D.** A session clip is the MidiClip or AudioClip element in a slot's ClipSlot/Value, with the attributes Id and Time (Time is 0 on every shipped session clip). Both classes start with the same 28 fields; then MidiClip holds Notes and its program and editor fields, and AudioClip holds SampleRef, Onsets, the warp fields, fades, pitch, SampleVolume and WarpMarkers. - **D.** Field owners: | Fields of the clip element | Owner | | --- | --- | | LaunchMode, LaunchQuantisation, Legato, VelocityAmount, FollowAction | [REQ-CLIP-LAUNCH-001](clip-launch.md#req-clidraftwiki/specs/live-set-structure.md
REQ-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE-008SPEC-LIVE-SET-STRUCTURE

REQ-MEDIA-FILE-001SPEC-MEDIA-FILE-WORKFLOWS
Draft spec		Audio import surface: **D12; exact-build U.** Documented mono/stereo native formats are WAV, AIFF, AIFF-C, FLAC and OGG Vorbis. MP3 is importable; M4A import is macOS-only. Uncompressed input need not be converted beforehand solely for its sample rate/bit depth/length. Codec profiles, container variants, channels beyond stereo and practical bounds remain U. Source sample-files.draftwiki/specs/media-file-workflows.md
REQ-MEDIA-FILE-002SPEC-MEDIA-FILE-WORKFLOWS
Draft spec		Compressed source and cache: **D12; exact-build U.** Compressed import writes decoded uncompressed WAV data to a temporary cache file under Cache/Decoding. Cache retention and PCM contents are distinct from source identity; decode quality, early-playback readiness and completion timing remain U. Source the-decoding-cache.draftwiki/specs/media-file-workflows.md
REQ-MEDIA-FILE-003SPEC-MEDIA-FILE-WORKFLOWS
Draft spec		Cache eviction controls: **D12; exact-build U.** Older decoded files are automatically removed to make space. Maximum Cache Size can impose a configured limit; Cleanup deletes cached files not used by the open Set. Eviction order, active-reference definition and locking/transactions remain U. Source the-decoding-cache.draftwiki/specs/media-file-workflows.md
REQ-MEDIA-FILE-004SPEC-MEDIA-FILE-WORKFLOWS
Draft spec		Free-space refusal: **D12; exact-build U.** Minimum Free Space controls reserved disk space. Source the-decoding-cache.draftwiki/specs/media-file-workflows.md
REQ-MEDIA-FILE-005SPEC-MEDIA-FILE-WORKFLOWS

Draft spec		pan law: - **X.** For one track, with input channels L, R, output channels L′, R′, track gain v (REQ-011), split weight w and θ(x) = (x + 1)·π/4: - L′ = v·(w·cos θ(sL) + (1 − w)·max(10⁻⁵, √2·cos θ(p)))·L + v·w·cos θ(sR)·R - R′ = v·w·sin θ(sL)·L + v·(w·sin θ(sR) + (1 − w)·max(10⁻⁵, √2·sin θ(p)))·R - v = 0 gives silence. Here p is the pan, sL and sR the split pans, and w the pan-mode amount. The matrix function 0x101b719e0 (arm64 0x101b3b95c) was run on these inputs and produced exactly the gains in MV-035 to MV-037. Draft spec		crossfade effect: - **S.** A track with crossfade assign None is not affected by the crossfader. - **S.** A track assigned A is scaled by T(c) and a track assigned B by T(−c), where c is the crossfader value and T is the selected crossfade curve, a 129-point table over [−1, 1] with linear interpolation. REQ-MPE-005SPEC-MPE-WORKFLOWS

REQ-MPE-006SPEC-MPE-WORKFLOWS
Draft spec		Drag a selected breakpoint or a selected line segment. REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-001SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS

REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-002SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Arpeggiator sequence styles: **D12 (M 0011–0020, 0026).** Style selects and displays a note pattern; previous and next buttons cycle styles. Play Order follows input play order; Chord Trigger repeats the held pitches together. Random continuously randomizes; Random Other avoids reusing a note until the others have been used; Random Once repeats one random ordering until incoming MIDI changes. Pattern Offset 1 starts at the second pattern position and moves the former first to last. **U:** exact orders for Up/Down/Converge/Diverge and all other styles, duplicate-pitch identity, random seed/distribution, what changes invalidraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-003SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Arpeggiator rate, gate and transposition: **D12 (M 0021–0024).** Rate is milliseconds in Free or a tempo-synced division. Gate expresses duration as a percentage of Rate; values over 100% overlap. Distance is semitones or scale degrees; Steps counts successive transpositions following the original pattern. Distance +12 st, Steps 2 gives original, +12, +24. Negative Distance lowers successive repetitions. Root/Scale choosers set local scale; Use Current Scale takes the clip scale and disables these choosers. **U:** first event phase, exact division catalog, timing grid, gate rounding, end-of-pattern overlaps, groove interaction and pitdraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-004SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Arpeggiator held set, retrigger and repetition: **D12 (M 0025, 0030–0035).** Hold keeps a pattern after physical release; adding held keys adds pitches and playing a pitch a second time removes it as described by the manual. Retrigger Off does not restart the pattern, Note restarts on a new note, Beat restarts at Interval; the retrigger LED flashes. Repeats controls pattern repetition; its documented default is infinite. **U:** replacement versus addition when all physical keys are up (the manual also says repetition continues until another key), pedal interaction, last-note removal, finite-repeat restart, transport stop/jump and held-note draftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-005SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Arpeggiator velocity and groove: **D12 (M 0027–0029, 0036–0037).** Groove selects swing influenced by Global Groove Amount. Velocity enables Target/Decay; Decay is the time to Target. REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-006SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		CC Control event families: **D12 (M 0041–0049).** The three fixed controls produce modulation, pitch bend and channel pressure; Pitch Bend has downward negative and upward positive values. Custom A switches between on/off or minimum/maximum and can be assigned through CC Type Chooser; CC64 sustain is its documented intended use. There are 12 customizable dials B–M. Pitch bend and pressure must be observed as their own MIDI event families, not assumed to be 7-bit CC messages. **U:** numeric ranges, wire encoding, channel choice, quantization, reset-to-center and repeated-value suppression; this source does not supply thedraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-007SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		CC Control assignment, Send and automation: **D12 (M 0050–0052).** B–M have custom names and assignments, shown on Push and saveable as presets. Values can be automated or moved in real time. Bank toggles show controls 1–8 or 9–16. Send outputs current MIDI CC values. Learn assigns incoming CC data to a customizable control. Existing CC automation and outgoing CC Control data merge. **U:** learning target selection, multi-message learning, consumption versus forwarding, Send order/count and treatment of non-CC fixed controls, duplicate assignments, same-time merge order, smoothing, preset-load emission and hardware receipt. Preset storadraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-008SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Chord pitches and duplicate shifts: **D12 (M 0056–0058).** An input note supplies the root and up to six additional pitches with Shift 1–6 in −36..+36 st. +4 and +7 form the root major triad, independent of which slots hold those values. Reassigning the same pitch to another Shift deactivates that additional assignment. **U:** zero-shift slot activation, collision with another input note, pitch overflow, note-off ownership and simultaneous ordering. **D12 (M 0057).** The LED next to each Shift knob flashes to indicate when its corresponding note is being played. This indicator role is not independent proof of delivered note evendraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-009SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Chord learning: **D12 (M 0059).** With Learn enabled, the first held key is the root and consumes no Shift; subsequent held pitches fill Shift slots in play order. REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-010SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Chord dynamics and chance: **D12 (M 0060–0063).** Each generated note has relative Velocity 1%..200%; 100% matches input velocity. No finite trial count is required to reproduce a probability proportion.draftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-011SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Chord strum, scale and per-note events: **D12 (M 0064–0073).** Strum offers delays up to 400 ms between notes; positive order is original then Shift1..Shift6, negative reverses it. The context option allows duplicate notes when strumming. Positive Tension accelerates successive strums; negative slows them. Crescendo raises or lowers successive velocities. Use Current Scale selects degree shifts. Send Per Note Events to Generated Notes extends MPE data to generated notes; with scale awareness, per-note bend follows the clip scale. **U:** delay curve/exact timestamps, tension/crescendo arithmetic, late note-offs during a pending strumdraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-012SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Note Length triggered on note-on: **D12 (M 0077–0078).** With Trigger Source Note On and Latch off, output duration is Length multiplied by Gate/100; Gate 50%, 100%, 200% yields half, full, double Length. Time Mode selects milliseconds or tempo divisions. **U:** exact start latency, source note-off suppression, same-key retrigger, gate/length control bounds and updating Length or tempo while an output note sounds.draftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-013SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Note Length triggered on note-off: **D12 (M 0079).** With Note Off selected, the output note starts when its input note is released, rather than at input note-on, and then uses Gate and Length. **U:** unpaired release, simultaneous releases, sustain's effect with Latch off, output note-off velocity and event-grid placement.draftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-014SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Note Length release dynamics: **D12 (M 0080–0083).** In Note Off mode, Release Velocity blends input on/off velocities. Decay begins at incoming note-on; its value at note-off sets output velocity, reaching zero after Decay Time. Positive Key Scale lengthens notes below C3 and shortens those above; negative reverses that relationship. **U:** blend equation, decay shape, order of operations, pitch scaling law and zero-velocity result. No numeric output oracle follows from the qualitative law.draftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-015SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Note Length latch: **D12 (M 0084).** Note On latch sustains triggered notes until the next note-on. Note Off latch depends on all keys/pedal being released and a new note-off. Latch disables Gate and Length; in Note Off latch, Release Velocity, Decay Time and Key Scale are also disabled. **U:** exact Note Off latch transition (especially which release qualifies), chord release ordering, pedal and repeated-note cases. The documented UI disablement is gradable; the ambiguous Note Off event sequence is not assigned a fabricated oracle.draftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-016SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Pitch transposition and step controls: **D12 (M 0088–0092).** Pitch offers ±128 st or ±30 scale degrees. Step Up/Down changes Pitch by Step Width, 1..48 st or 1..30 degrees. REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-017SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Pitch range modes: **D12 (M 0093–0097).** Lowest and Range define permitted pitches. Block drops out-of-range notes and flashes its LED; Fold transposes them into range; Limit moves below-range notes to the lower bound and above-range notes to the upper bound. **U:** range width/end inclusion, filtering before versus after Pitch, Fold interval and empty/one-note range. REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-018SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Random pitch selection and signs: **D12 (M 0101–0104, 0107–0114).** Chance controls probability of pitch alteration; Choices has 1..24 possibilities and Interval controls their spacing. Add raises, Sub lowers, Bi permits both; the +/0/− LEDs identify the direction. The documented Random/Add example Choices 1, Interval 12, Chance 50% restricts outputs to C3 or C4 for input C3. Choices12/Interval1 permits unaltered C3 or C#3..C4. **U:** seed/distribution, finite proportions, exact Chance thresholds, Bi zero handling and overflow. The examples authorize pitch-membership predicates only, not a fixed random sequence or a 50/50 finidraftwiki/specs/native-midi-effects.md
REQ-NATIVE-MIDI-019SPEC-NATIVE-MIDI-EFFECTS
Draft spec		Random Alt mode and contradictory examples: **D12 (M 0105).** Alt uses a cyclic order. Chance100% advances to the next step; Chance0% outputs the incoming pitch. **U (M 0106):** a 12-choice example describes C3 through C4 before reset (13 notes), while Choices2/Interval2 describes only C3,D3 (2 notes). If the derivation is wrong, discovery could crash repeatedly.draftwiki/specs/plugin-discovery.md
REQ-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY-013SPEC-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY
Draft spec		hanging module: - **U.** No time limit on examining a module was found, so a module that never returns may stall discovery indefinitely. No reference observation is available (ADR 0003; formerly PRB-H1-03, PRB-N4-05). Static route: what the scanner's watchdog constants govern (appendix row 013).draftwiki/specs/plugin-discovery.md
REQ-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY-014SPEC-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY
Draft spec		many new modules: - **U.** Whether one scan with more than 50 new modules lists all of them without further user action. No reference observation is available (ADR 0003; formerly PRB-H1-04, PRB-N4-02), and no further static route is known. REQ-003's order between the formats depends on it. - The derivation splits discovery into batches of at most 51 newly examined modules per format, restarted automatically. Batching is not a requirement.draftwiki/specs/plugin-discovery.md
REQ-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY-015SPEC-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY
Draft spec		duplicates: - **U.** Two cases are unresolved: the same bundle present in two folders, and two modules declaring the same plug-in class ID. Unknown: whether each appears once or twice, and which one is used. No reference observation is available (ADR 0003; formerly PRB-H1-08). Static route: how Live builds the plug-in list from the stored results (appendix row 015).draftwiki/specs/plugin-discovery.md
REQ-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY-016SPEC-PLUGIN-DISCOVERY
Draft spec		quitting during a scan: - **S.** If the application quits during a scan, discovery does not run to completion. - **S.** At the next scan, modules whose examination completed before the quit are not examined again, and the remaining ones are examined. - **U.** How long examination continues after the quit. No reference observation is available (ADR 0003). Static route: the interval of the scanner's check for its parent process (appendix row 016).draftwiki/specs/plugin-discovery.md

REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-001SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		input and arm selection: **D12, R19 §19.1–19.2.** A track records the input selected in its In/Out controls. Audio inputs can be mono/stereo; MIDI input can select device/channel; another track can be the source. Session and Arrangement Arm controls address the same tracks. In the documented ordinary arm operation, clicking one Arm disarms other tracks; Ctrl on Windows/Cmd on macOS allows multiple arms. For multiple selected tracks, clicking an Arm arms the other selected tracks. Arming selects the track. **U:** preference-dependent exceptions, implicit arm, frozen/nonrecordable tracks and arm changes during recordingdraftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-002SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		input monitoring: **D12, R17 §17.1.** Auto passes input when armed and inhibits monitoring while clips play. In continuously passes input and suppresses clip output regardless of arm. Off disables monitoring; it permits recording with external monitoring. A Monitor choice applies to all selected tracks. This clause specifies a selection/gating result, not a latency or signal-processing tolerance. **U:** factory/new-track defaults: R19 §19.2 calls monitoring of armed tracks the default, while R17 §17.1 describes reset defaults of Off for audio and Auto for MIDI. Preserve the contextual distinction; do not imposedraftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-003SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		Arrangement record start: **D12, R19 §19.3.1.** With Start Playback with Record enabled, Arrangement Record starts recording. Disabled, Record waits for Play or a Session clip launch. Shift while pressing Record reverses that preference's behavior. Recording creates clips on armed tracks. **U:** exact scheduler order at the start event and pressing Record again before the delayed start.draftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-004SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		Arrangement MIDI overdub: **D12, R19 §19.3.1.** With MIDI Arrangement Overdub enabled, a new MIDI clip combines the track's existing MIDI signal and new input. The function applies to MIDI tracks. It does not define an audio overdub operation. **U:** overlapping same-pitch note merge/retrigger rules and exact behavior with Overdub disabled.draftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-005SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		punch gates: **D12, R19 §19.3.1.** Enabled Punch-In prevents recording before the Arrangement loop start. Enabled Punch-Out prevents recording after its loop end. These allow a pre-roll without recording over protected material. **U:** ownership of an event exactly at either endpoint, held-note splitting, sample alignment and moving the loop/punch points during recording.draftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-006SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		retention across audio loop passes: **D12, R19 §19.3.1.** Arrangement loop recording retains audio across passes. The resulting sample can contain the whole recorded run; Clip View's loop brace selects the last pass and moving its markers can audition prior passes. The manual also describes repeated Undo to unroll the recording. Take-lane creation is REQ-018. **U:** partial last passes, segmentation between files, pass-specific Undo granularity and disk reclamation.draftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-007SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		Session slot record and playback: **D12, R19 §19.3.2.** Empty slots on armed tracks show record controls. Session Record records the selected scene in armed tracks; the recording clip has a red launch control. Pressing Session Record again changes recording to loop playback. A slot's record control starts that slot; its launch control changes it to loop playback. Clip Stop or transport Stop stops the clip. A non-None Global Quantization is the documented setup for musically cut clips. **U:** exact recording start/end scheduling and occupied-slot behavior.draftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-008SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		scene launch and New: **D12, R19 §19.3.2.** By default a scene launch does not record its empty armed slots; Start Recording on Scene Launch enables that behavior. New stops clips in armed tracks and selects a scene available for new recordings, creating a scene when needed. The captured manual exposes New in Key/MIDI Map Mode. **U:** the scene-search ordering and interaction with follow actions.draftwiki/specs/recording-comping.md
REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-009SPEC-RECORDING-COMPING
Draft spec		Session MIDI overdub: **D12, R19 §19.3.3.** In an armed MIDI track with a looping clip, Session Record adds played notes on successive passes. Further presses toggle between overdub and playback so rehearsal input is not added while overdub is off. Undo can remove the last take while overdubbing; note editing remains available. **U:** precise take grouping, duplicate-note handling and Undo while a note is held.
